aboutMeta: About Reikun (例訓) — Semantic Japanese Dictionary & Reading Assistant: bilingual search, sentence breakdowns with furigana, kanji stroke order, and JLPT-calibrated grammar explanations.
aboutLede: Reikun (例訓) is a free, open-source Japanese reading assistant — a semantic dictionary that works in both English and Japanese.
searchText: look up words in English or Japanese; natural-language questions ("how do you say X") are rewritten into dictionary terms automatically.
breakdownText: paste a Japanese sentence and it is split into word units with furigana, per-word glosses, and hover detail.
kanjiText: readings, meanings, common compounds, JLPT level, and animated stroke-order diagrams.
grammarText: concise explanations calibrated to a JLPT level (N5–N1), generated on demand by a LLM provider.
liteVsFullText: Lite is a plain, JavaScript-free version of the same dictionary: no popups, animations or grammar explanations, so it also works in text browsers and on slow connections. Theme, language and recent searches carry over between the two.
howText: Search runs hybrid retrieval — dense vector embeddings plus BM25 — fused in Qdrant, with query routing that picks the right plan for English words, English sentences, and Japanese input. Sentence parsing uses the Sudachi morphological analyzer; embeddings are quantized ONNX models running on CPU. The frontend is a static SvelteKit site; the API is a FastAPI service.

privacyText: No accounts and no cross-site tracking. Search queries are logged to improve the dictionary; feedback and explanation text is stored only as one-way hashes. Theme, language, furigana and recent searches stay on your device.
